tasks.trap: 5-table join; Q1 end edge (order 5 at 2026-03-31 23:59 vs BETWEEN ... '2026-03-31'); charged unit_price vs list_price
tasks.question: For paid orders placed in Q1 2026 (January 1 through March 31, inclusive), what is the revenue per customer city and product category? Revenue is the quantity times the unit price charged on the order line. Show the city, the category name and the revenue.
tasks.reference: SELECT cu.city, ca.name AS category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN customers cu ON cu.id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id JOIN categories ca ON ca.id = p.category_id WHERE o.status = 'paid' AND o.created_at >= '2026-01-01' AND o.created_at < '2026-04-01' GROUP BY cu.city, ca.name
tasks.good:
```sql
SELECT cu.city, ca.name AS category, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS revenue
FROM orders o
JOIN customers cu ON cu.id = o.customer_id
JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id
JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
JOIN categories ca ON ca.id = p.category_id
WHERE o.status = 'paid'
  AND date(o.created_at) BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-03-31'
GROUP BY cu.city, ca.name
ORDER BY revenue DESC;
```
Revenue per city and category for paid Q1 orders.

tasks.trap: NULL handling: AVG(discount) skips NULL discounts (0.10 instead of 0.0556)
tasks.question: What is the average discount across all paid orders? Orders with no discount recorded should count as a discount of 0.
tasks.reference: SELECT AVG(COALESCE(discount, 0)) AS avg_discount FROM orders WHERE status = 'paid'
tasks.good:
```sql
SELECT AVG(COALESCE(o.discount, 0)) AS avg_discount
FROM orders o
WHERE o.status = 'paid';
```

tasks.question: Which customers have at least 3 paid orders and more than 2,200 in total paid revenue? Show the customer name, the number of paid orders and the total paid revenue (quantity times the line unit price).
tasks.reference: SELECT c.name, COUNT(DISTINCT o.id) AS paid_orders, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id AND o.status = 'paid' JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id GROUP BY c.id HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.id) >= 3 AND SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 2200
tasks.good:
```sql
SELECT c.name, COUNT(DISTINCT o.id) AS paid_orders, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS total_revenue
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id
WHERE o.status = 'paid'
GROUP BY c.id, c.name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT o.id) >= 3 AND SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) > 2200;
```

tasks.trap: top-N per group (window function); a global LIMIT 2 returns 2 rows instead of 6; refunded/pending lines must not count
tasks.question: For each product category, list its 2 best-selling products by units sold in paid orders, with the units sold. Products with no paid sales are not listed, and a category with fewer than 2 such products shows only what it has.
tasks.reference: SELECT category, product, units FROM (SELECT ca.name AS category, p.name AS product, SUM(oi.quantity) AS units, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ca.id ORDER BY SUM(oi.quantity) DESC) AS rn FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id AND o.status = 'paid' JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id JOIN categories ca ON ca.id = p.category_id GROUP BY ca.id, p.id) WHERE rn <= 2
tasks.good:
```sql
WITH sales AS (
  SELECT ca.name AS category, p.name AS product, SUM(oi.quantity) AS units
  FROM order_items oi
  JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
  JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
  JOIN categories ca ON ca.id = p.category_id
  WHERE o.status = 'paid'
  GROUP BY ca.name, p.name
), ranked AS (
  SELECT *, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY units DESC) AS rnk FROM sales
)
SELECT category, product, units FROM ranked WHERE rnk <= 2 ORDER BY category, units DESC;
```
bad:
```sql
SELECT ca.name AS category, p.name AS product, SUM(oi.quantity) AS units
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
JOIN categories ca ON ca.id = p.category_id
WHERE o.status = 'paid'
GROUP BY ca.name, p.name
ORDER BY units DESC
LIMIT 2;
```

```sql
SELECT category, product, units FROM (
  SELECT ca.name AS category, p.name AS product, SUM(oi.quantity) AS units,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY ca.id ORDER BY SUM(oi.quantity) DESC) AS rn
  FROM order_items oi
  JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
  JOIN categories ca ON ca.id = p.category_id
  GROUP BY ca.id, p.id
) WHERE rn <= 2;
```

tasks.trap: ambiguous columns: `status` is on orders AND shipments, `name` on three tables; 'returned' is a SHIPMENT status, not the refunded ORDER status
tasks.question: Which customers had a shipment with status 'returned', and which carrier handled it? Show the customer name and the carrier, one row per distinct customer and carrier.
tasks.reference: SELECT DISTINCT c.name, s.carrier FROM shipments s JOIN orders o ON o.id = s.order_id JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE s.status = 'returned'
tasks.good:
```sql
SELECT DISTINCT c.name AS customer, s.carrier
FROM shipments s
JOIN orders o ON o.id = s.order_id
JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id
WHERE s.status = 'returned'
ORDER BY customer, s.carrier;
```
bad:
```sql
SELECT DISTINCT name, carrier
FROM shipments
JOIN orders ON orders.id = shipments.order_id
JOIN customers ON customers.id = orders.customer_id
WHERE status = 'returned';
```

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT c.name AS customer, s.carrier
FROM shipments s
JOIN orders o ON o.id = s.order_id
JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id
WHERE o.status = 'refunded';
```

tasks.trap: LEFT JOIN to keep zero categories (Training has no products, Accessories only sold in a cancelled order); a WHERE on the paid filter or a NULL sum loses the zeros
tasks.question: For every product category, how many units were sold in paid orders? Include categories that sold zero units, showing 0 for them.
tasks.reference: SELECT c.name, COALESCE(SUM(x.quantity), 0) AS units FROM categories c LEFT JOIN (SELECT p.category_id, oi.quantity FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id AND o.status = 'paid' JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id) x ON x.category_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id
tasks.good:
```sql
SELECT c.name AS category,
       COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN o.status = 'paid' THEN oi.quantity END), 0) AS units_sold
FROM categories c
LEFT JOIN products p ON p.category_id = c.id
LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON oi.product_id = p.id
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name
ORDER BY units_sold DESC;
```
bad:

tasks.trap: self-join on customers.referred_by, plus a cross-row predicate (different city)
tasks.question: List every customer who was referred by another customer living in a different city. Show the referred customer's name, the referrer's name, and both of their cities.
tasks.reference: SELECT c.name AS customer, r.name AS referrer, c.city, r.city AS referrer_city FROM customers c JOIN customers r ON r.id = c.referred_by WHERE c.city <> r.city
tasks.good:
```sql
SELECT c.name AS customer, c.city AS customer_city, r.name AS referrer, r.city AS referrer_city
FROM customers c
JOIN customers r ON r.id = c.referred_by
WHERE c.city != r.city
ORDER BY c.name;
```
bad:
```sql
SELECT c.name AS customer, c.city AS customer_city, r.name AS referrer, r.city AS referrer_city
FROM customers c
JOIN customers r ON r.id = c.referred_by;
```

```sql
SELECT c.name AS customer, c.city AS customer_city, r.name AS referrer, r.city AS referrer_city
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN customers r ON r.id = c.referred_by
WHERE r.id IS NULL OR c.city != r.city;
```
